C1:
Problem 1: Humanoid:MoveTo has an 8-second timeout. If the goal isn't reached by then, the humanoid stops walking and MoveToFinished fires anyway, with reached = false. Your code ignores that argument, so it prints "arrived". Fix: `local reached = hum.MoveToFinished:Wait()` and check it. For long trips, call MoveTo again on each waypoint, which resets the timer.
Problem 2: MoveTo walks in a straight line and knows nothing about obstacles. Fix: use PathfindingService.
```lua
local path = PathfindingService:CreatePath({AgentRadius=2, AgentHeight=5, AgentCanJump=true})
local ok = pcall(path.ComputeAsync, path, root.Position, target.Position)
if ok and path.Status == Enum.PathStatus.Success then
  for _, wp in path:GetWaypoints() do
    if wp.Action == Enum.PathWaypointAction.Jump then hum.Jump = true end
    hum:MoveTo(wp.Position)
    if not hum.MoveToFinished:Wait() then break end -- recompute
  end
end
```
Also listen to path.Blocked and recompute the path. A moving target needs a fresh path every so often. Call root:SetNetworkOwner(nil) so the server owns the NPC and its movement doesn't stutter.
C2: Each time the character respawns, every ScreenGui with ResetOnSpawn = true (the default) is destroyed and re-cloned from StarterGui into PlayerGui. Your LocalScript inside it is destroyed with it, so its local variables are lost, and the new copy starts from the defaults. Fixes: (1) set ScreenGui.ResetOnSpawn = false so the GUI and its script stay alive, or (2) keep the settings somewhere that outlives the GUI: a ModuleScript or LocalScript under StarterPlayerScripts, or attributes on the Player, and re-apply them when the GUI is created. To keep settings across sessions, send them to the server (validated) and save them in a DataStore. Also don't parent long-lived state scripts under StarterCharacterScripts, which reset the same way.
C3: Animations replicate from a client only when that client is the network owner of the rig: its own character, through Humanoid/AnimationController > Animator. That's why the sword swing replicates. The shopkeeper NPC belongs to the server, so animations a client plays on it stay local and nobody else sees them. For the second NPC, the Animator was made with Instance.new on the client, so it exists only on that client and doesn't replicate. Fix: play NPC animations from a server Script, using the Animator that the server created (or that ships in the model): `npc.Humanoid.Animator:LoadAnimation(anim):Play()`. Server-played animations replicate to everyone. Alternative: fire a RemoteEvent to all clients and have each client play it locally. Never create the Animator on the client. On the server, Humanoid:WaitForChild("Animator") or create it there. The animation asset must be owned by the experience owner (user or group), or it won't load.
C4:
(1) A Sound whose parent is Workspace (or SoundService or the GUI) has no position, so it plays globally at full volume for everyone. Fix: parent it to the barrel's Part or an Attachment so it becomes positional, and set RollOffMaxDistance. Or have the server clone it into the barrel and Play it there, then clean it up (Debris, or Ended -> Destroy).
(2) Positional volume fades with distance according to RollOffMode and RollOffMinDistance/RollOffMaxDistance. Past RollOffMaxDistance the sound is silent. Fix: raise RollOffMaxDistance (and RollOffMinDistance) and use RollOffMode Inverse/InverseTapered, or Linear for a predictable fade. Optionally add a second, global siren on the client.
(3) Loaded fires only once. If the sound has already loaded before you call Wait, the event never fires again and the script hangs. Fix: `if not siren.IsLoaded then siren.Loaded:Wait() end` (ideally with a timeout), or just call Play(), which starts the sound when it loads. You can also preload with ContentProvider:PreloadAsync.
C5:
Two bugs. (1) workspace:Raycast's second argument is a direction vector, and its length is the ray's range. A .Unit vector is only 1 stud long, so the ray almost never hits anything and returns nil. Indexing result.Instance then errors. (2) The ray starts inside your own head, and with no RaycastParams it hits your own character. Fix:
```lua
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {player.Character}
local origin = head.Position
local dir = (mouseHit - origin).Unit * 500 -- range
local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
if result then print(result.Instance.Name, result.Position) end
```
Always check result for nil. Get mouseHit from Mouse.Hit.Position, or from camera:ViewportPointToRay plus your own ray. Add tool and accessory parts to the filter if they still get hit. For a real gun, send only the shot to the server and redo the raycast and validation there. Never trust the client to report a hit.
C6:
Two tweens on the same property of the same instance conflict. Starting the click tween cancels the hover tween that is still running (the newest tween wins). The hover's Completed then fires with Cancelled, and any follow-up logic runs from a half-finished value. Restoring "back" to a value captured mid-tween leaves the button in odd states. Structure: keep one source of truth for the button's state (hovered, pressed) and one active tween per property. Store the current tween, Cancel() it before you create a new one, and always tween toward a target computed from the state, not from the current value:
```lua
local current
local function go(t, props) if current then current:Cancel() end current = TweenService:Create(btn, TweenInfo.new(t), props) current:Play() end
local function target() return hovered and 0.2 or 0.5 end
btn.MouseEnter:Connect(function() hovered=true go(0.3,{BackgroundTransparency=target()}) end)
btn.MouseLeave:Connect(function() hovered=false go(0.3,{BackgroundTransparency=target()}) end)
btn.Activated:Connect(function() go(0.05,{BackgroundTransparency=0}) task.delay(0.05,function() go(0.15,{BackgroundTransparency=target()}) end) end)
```
Better still, animate the flash on a separate property or a child overlay frame (or a UIScale) so it never fights the hover tween.

Use a MemoryStoreSortedMap keyed by skill bucket or rating (with sort keys) for the skill-sorted queue, or a MemoryStoreQueue (ReadAsync invisibility, then RemoveAsync) for FIFO. Put leader leases in a MemoryStoreHashMap. Limits: memory quota = 64 KB + 1.2 KB x users, and writes past it fail with TotalMemoryOverLimit. Requests are 1,000 + 120 x CCU units per minute for the whole experience. Each partition takes about 30,000 units/min, and one sorted map or queue is one partition, so shard hot structures. Values are up to 32 KB and keys up to 128 characters. Expiration is 45 days at most (3,888,000 s) and is required on Queue adds. Each queue or map holds at most 1M items / 100 MB. GetRangeAsync returns up to 200 items; Queue ReadAsync up to 100. Design: data is temporary, so give tickets short TTLs and refresh them. A party is one ticket. Elect one matchmaker per queue with a hash-map lease (renew about every 5 s, TTL about 15 s). Use UpdateAsync for atomic claims. Read items reappear after the invisibility timeout (about 30 s), so make the steps idempotent. Wrap every call in pcall with backoff. Then ReserveServerAsync plus TeleportAsync, and announce matches with MessagingService if needed. Widen the skill range the longer a ticket waits.
